parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the prompt as a complete Pylama 8.4.1 build with package files, tests, docs, packaging, linter integrations, API exports, hooks, and official scoring by tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It used one AgentSwarm call with four scoped children: core package/tests, pylint compatibility, packaging/root files, and docs/CI extras; the parent retained final integration and acceptance work.
parallel.implementation: Children copied most of the reference tree and made scoped changes; the parent added setup.cfg paths, API aliases in errors.py, hook.py behavior, and a final check_paths/rootdir change in main.py.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the completed swarm result, reconciled the core-child setup.cfg failure, and edited shared files itself after children returned, but the run ended without a final delivery message.
parallel.verification: Parallel got 35 local tests passing, then ran API/smoke checks that exposed additional issues; after the final main.py edit there is no observed rerun of the tests or smoke checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation completed at 32/34 and the agent process timed out; the last implementation edit was not followed by verification or a final completion response.

serial.requirements: The serial agent reconstructed the same required project surface, including full package layout, exported API, packaging, tests, docs, CLI modes, hooks, and optional linter integrations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept all implementation, integration, packaging, and verification in one main-agent sequence with no child agents or delegation boundaries.
serial.implementation: It copied the real Pylama project, patched __init__.py exports, pytest 8 path handling, setup.cfg package lists and paths, dummy.py pylint compatibility, Error methods, and hook APIs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor owned the full tree, setup/config/test compatibility fixes were applied directly and then cleaned up before the final response.
serial.verification: It reran the full test suite after late fixes, ran API smoke tests, CLI checks, and wheel packaging checks, then reran the tests once more after cleanup.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation also failed 32/34 despite local 35-test success; within the trajectory it completed normally and reported no remaining local issue.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the complete Pylama package, CLI, config, linter, reporting, async, hook, docs, and test obligations from the shared prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same complete Pylama requirements and expected source tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both used upstream Pylama 8.4.1 as their implementation base.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the project into four child scopes and kept parent-level integration, including later setup.cfg and API fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did all copying, patching, testing, and packaging checks in one non-delegated main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main difference is a multi-agent scoped build with later parent integration versus a single-owner sequential build.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs included explicit file ownership, polling rules, and validation expectations; agent 0 reported the setup.cfg path issue to the parent rather than silently hiding it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained all interface knowledge in one context and patched exports, config, hooks, and pytest compatibility without cross-agent handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used explicit handoffs and scoped ownership, creating an integration stage, while serial avoided handoff interpretation by keeping the whole tree in one agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated copied sources, setup.cfg paths, Error aliases, hook changes, and then a final main.py rootdir change for check_paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made analogous source/config/API/hook changes, including dummy.py pylint compatibility and final package behavior checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementations converged on similar substance, but the parallel main.py edit came after earlier verification and did not get a closing check.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four child results returned to the parent through the AgentSwarm aggregate, and the parent proceeded with integration work afterward.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the main agent kept direct control and produced a final completion response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not lose child outputs, but its own final implementation lifecycle ended with cancellation after a parent edit.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared one workspace but used scoped children and parent integration; no direct same-file overwrite or live write collision is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final workspace in one sequence, avoiding cross-agent provenance questions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material shared-state difference is not a write collision; it is that parent integration continued after child work and later verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel obtained a full local test pass, then found and fixed API issues, but no verification follows the final main.py edit.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reran the full suite after late fixes, ran smoke checks, checked the wheel, cleaned build artifacts, and reran the suite again.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed verification after the last material changes; parallel left its final material change unverifiable in-trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the full run budget and timed out; the terminal raw event is cancellation shortly after the final implementation edit.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout and with 570 seconds remaining, then emitted a final completion report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel closure state was budget-forced and unverified after the last edit, while serial reached normal closure after verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed evaluations report solution_passed false with 32 of 34 tests passing. The main contrast is process closure, not score: parallel left a final parent implementation edit unverified after earlier local tests and API checks, while serial reran tests and smoke checks after its late changes and completed normally.
parallel_contributors: Post-verification main.py edit followed immediately by cancellation left the final artifact without in-trajectory validation.
serial_contributors: Sequential ownership allowed the final late fixes to be followed by full tests, smoke checks, wheel inspection, cleanup, and another test run.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both official results have the same 32/34 aggregate; the allowed inputs do not expose the two hidden failing test identities, so no unique implementation root cause is claimed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast and retained parallel adverse state only

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicitly assigned to agent 0 for the core package/tests and agent 1 for the pylint linter, with the parent continuing integration.
The parent inspected the returned swarm result, edited setup.cfg and source files, and acted as integration owner after children completed.
Packaging and root files were owned by agent 2 and the final workspace contained setup.py, setup.cfg, package files, tests, docs, and root support files.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition from child outputs through integrated tests and later API fixes; the problem was timing of a final edit, not owner absence.
The parent explored before delegation, but productive implementation was then delegated and performed by four children rather than blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight.
The run did not complete a separate all-investigation phase before implementation; child implementation and validation scopes ran through the swarm and returned concrete work.

The indispensable integration path was owned and active after the swarm; the terminal issue is a post-verification edit without a closing check, not evidence that capacity was allocated away from that path.
Four children and a timeout are visible, but child breadth alone is not enough; all child results returned and the direct realized boundary is the later unverified parent edit.

Agent 0 had the broadest scope and left one test failure, but it returned usable work and the parent corrected the issue; the final unverified change was made by the parent, not left inside an oversized child scope.

The child briefs included their scoped acceptance tests and file boundaries; the setup.cfg paths issue was discovered during child execution and then fixed by the parent, not a known omitted requirement at delegation.

The setup.cfg and test interaction caused temporary parent reconciliation, but there is no lasting incompatible component set; the parent consumed the report and integrated the config fix before later verification.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer; agent 0's remaining setup.cfg issue and other child results were returned to the parent.
The AgentSwarm return was lengthy but the parent used it, fixed setup.cfg, and continued with API checks; no needed result is shown materially unconsumed because of bulk.
No child or parent acted on a handoff that described a superseded workspace state; later parent edits were based on current direct checks.
The child reports did not present incompatible contracts that remained unadjudicated; the only reported conflict-like issue was resolved by parent integration.
The parent did not make a final whole-task completion or acceptance statement after the last main.py edit; the run was cancelled before closure, so the direct timing label is more specific.
There is no replacement or retry child that repeats prior work without inherited checkpoint state; the parallel run used one swarm and no retried child.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child is shown being explicitly stopped before needed work or results finalized; all four AgentSwarm children returned completed reports.
The final problem is not failure to promote a complete candidate; the candidate was already in the workspace and then changed after relevant verification.
After integrated tests and later API checks, the parent edited pylama/main.py and the next observed terminal event is cancellation, with no test or smoke check after that merge.
candidates.realized_consequence: The final main.py implementation change entered the delivered workspace in an unverifiable state because no post-merge test or smoke-check result exists before cancellation.
candidates.near_match_reason: Late Finalization is wrong because the artifact was already assembled and then modified; the observed error is an unclosed verification loop after a merge.

candidates.reason: Completed child implementation was not left unjoined; the AgentSwarm aggregate returned and the parent used child work before continuing with integrated checks.
No verifier child produced a trapped concrete finding; verification was run by implementation children and the parent, and those outputs were visible.
No required child failed or was cancelled without takeover; agent 0 returned its remaining issue and the parent took over setup.cfg integration.
The parent inspected and acted on child results, including the setup.cfg paths failure from agent 0; no completed child result is shown ignored at a decision point.
The parent was actively reading files, running checks, and editing source near timeout; it did not simply wait blindly on available progress or results.
Children had distinct file scopes and the parent later integrated fixes; no competing cross-file designs claiming the same behavior remained unresolved.
No two live agents are shown editing the same file and observing or reconciling each other's concurrent modification; parent edits occurred after child returns.
No actor wholesale replaced or deleted source produced by another active owner; scoped source work and later parent edits were integration, not proven overwrite.
There was no direct executable or submitted artifact replacement while another agent owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another agent's final-tree work or provenance.
The shared workspace did not by itself cause a proven unstable-state or provenance problem; ownership scopes were explicit and no more specific write collision is evidenced.
No generated cache, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor is shown being consumed by another as stable reference input; the shared reference source was intended.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The timeout-adjacent alternatives Late Finalization, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Load Imbalance variants were suppressed because the directly evidenced boundary is the post-verification main.py edit followed by cancellation without recheck.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no other candidate had both a directly evidenced parallel coordination boundary and an independent realized consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained pattern is one episode with a unique consequence and evidence set; the analysis does not add labels for child count, normal handoffs, shared workspace use, or timeout alone.
